Cylinder (geometry)

Words: 57
Geometry and topology OurBigBook.com
A cylinder is generated by translating a plane curve along parallel lines transverse to its plane. A circular cylinder uses a circle as its generating plane curve; it is right when the generators are perpendicular to that plane. The term can denote the lateral surface or, for a bounded portion with end caps, the enclosed solid. The circular cylinder curvature formulas describe the smooth lateral surface.

Parametric equation

Words: 39
Geometry and topology OurBigBook.com
A parametric equation expresses coordinates as functions of one or more independent parameters. For example, x=cost, y=sint describes a circle; multiple parameters describe surfaces. A smooth curve is a differentiable single-parameter realization. A reparametrization changes the parameter without changing the geometric image.

Embedding

Words: 38
Geometry and topology OurBigBook.com
An embedding identifies one mathematical structure with a structure-preserving copy inside another. In topology it is a homeomorphism onto its image with the subspace topology; an algebraic embedding is an injective homomorphism. A smooth embedding additionally has injective differential everywhere, so its image is an embedded submanifold.

Pencil (geometry)

Words: 43
Geometry and topology OurBigBook.com
A pencil is a one-parameter linear family of geometric objects. For linearly independent homogeneous polynomials F,G of equal degree, sF+tG=0, indexed by [s:t]∈P1, is a pencil of plane curves or hypersurfaces. Lines through a fixed point give a simple example; a pencil of plane curves specializes the general construction.

Spherical geometry

Words: 474 Articles: 9
Geometry and topology OurBigBook.com
Spherical geometry studies distances and angles intrinsically on a sphere. On the unit sphere, the shorter great circle arc between non-antipodal points with unit position vectors u,v has length arccos(u⋅v).

Convex regular spherical polygon (nn−2​π<α<π)

Words: 62
Spherical geometry OurBigBook.com
A nondegenerate convex regular spherical n-gon contained in an open hemisphere has equal interior angles α in the displayed interval. The spherical excess formula gives area nα−(n−2)π>0. Conversely, put equally spaced vertices at colatitude t∈(0,π/2) around a pole. Dividing each central triangle in half gives cot(α/2)=costtan(π/n) by the spherical law of cosines. As t increases, the angle ranges continuously from the Euclidean limiting angle to π.

Spherical circle (C(r)=2πRsin(r/R))

Words: 65
Spherical geometry OurBigBook.com
On a sphere of radius R, a spherical circle of radius r∈(0,πR) is the locus at spherical distance r from its center. Its polar angle about that center is r/R, so parametrization by longitude has speed Rsin(r/R). Its circumference is therefore 2πRsin(r/R). For small r, this is 2πr−πr3/(3R2)+O(r5), with the deficit determined by the sphere's positive Gaussian curvature.

Spherical lune

Words: 42
Spherical geometry OurBigBook.com
A spherical lune is the region between two great semicircles joining antipodal points. On a unit sphere a lune of opening angle α has area 2α, obtained by integrating area over longitude width α. Lune area counting yields the spherical excess formula.

Great-circle distance (d(u,v)=Rarccos(u⋅v))

Words: 61
Spherical geometry OurBigBook.com
For points on a sphere of radius R, write their position vectors relative to the centre as Ru,Rv with u,v unit vectors. The great-circle distance is the shorter great circle arc length, R times its central angle. Hence it equals Rarccos(u⋅v), including zero for identical points and πR for antipodal points. At antipodal points the shortest arc is not unique, but its length is.

Spherical trigonometry

Words: 90 Articles: 2
Spherical geometry OurBigBook.com
Spherical trigonometry relates side lengths and angles of spherical triangles. Side lengths are measured as central angles, or equivalently arc lengths on the unit sphere.

Spherical law of sines (sinA/sina=sinB/sinb=sinC/sinc)

Words: 26
Spherical trigonometry OurBigBook.com
For a nondegenerate convex minor spherical triangle, its scalar triple product τ=u⋅(v×w) satisfies ∣τ∣=sinbsincsinA, and cyclically. Dividing by sinasinbsinc proves the spherical law of sines.

Spherical law of cosines (cosa=cosbcosc+sinbsinccosA)

Words: 43
Spherical trigonometry OurBigBook.com
For a convex minor spherical triangle with opposite side-angle pairs (a,A),(b,B),(c,C), the displayed identity is the spherical law of cosines. At a vertex with unit position vector u, the two outgoing unit tangent vectors are (v−(u⋅v)u)/sinc and (w−(u⋅w)u)/sinb. Taking their dot product gives the identity.

Spherical triangle

Words: 128 Articles: 1
Spherical geometry OurBigBook.com
A spherical triangle is bounded by three great circle arcs. For the usual convex minor triangle, the vertices are neither antipodal nor on one great circle, and its sides and interior angles lie in (0,π).

Spherical triangle reflection group (∣G∣=1/p+1/q+1/r−14​)

Words: 97
Spherical triangle OurBigBook.com
Reflections in the sides of a spherical triangle of angles π/p,π/q,π/r generate a finite group when its images tessellate the sphere. The triangle area is π(1/p+1/q+1/r−1) by the spherical excess formula. Label its three vertex types and continue those labels across each reflected side; they are consistent around every vertex and, because the sphere is simply connected, globally. The generated group preserves these labels, so a chamber stabilizer fixes all three vertices and is trivial. Dividing sphere area by chamber area gives its order. Up to permutation the possibilities are (2,2,n) for n≥2, and (2,3,3),(2,3,4),(2,3,5), of orders 4n,24,48,120.

Convex geometry

Words: 178 Articles: 4
Geometry and topology OurBigBook.com
The study of convex sets, their convex hulls, supporting closed half-spaces, and inequalities for their sizes.

Minkowski addition (A+B)

Words: 165 Articles: 3
Convex geometry OurBigBook.com
The Minkowski sum of subsets A,B of a vector space is A+B={a+b:a∈A,b∈B}. Minkowski addition also makes sense for nonconvex sets; translations and positive dilations commute with it.

Sum of two closed sets need not be closed

Words: 46
Minkowski addition OurBigBook.com
In R, the sets X={n:n≥1} and Y={−n+1/n:n≥1} are closed because their points have no finite accumulation point. Their Minkowski sum contains 1/n→0 but does not contain zero, since m−n+1/n=0 has no positive-integer solution. Compactness of one summand is a useful sufficient condition missing from this counterexample.

Sum of a compact set and a closed set

Words: 59
Minkowski addition OurBigBook.com
In Euclidean space, a Minkowski sum of a compact set X and a closed set Y is closed. From any convergent sequence xj​+yj​, extract a convergent subsequence of xj​ using compactness. The corresponding yj​ then converges to the difference of the two limits, which lies in Y. If Y is also bounded, the sum is bounded and therefore compact.

Brunn-Minkowski theorem (λn​(A+B)1/n≥λn​(A)1/n+λn​(B)1/n)

Words: 36
Minkowski addition OurBigBook.com
For nonempty open sets A,B⊂Rn, the Lebesgue measure of their Minkowski sum satisfies
λn​(A+B)1/n≥λn​(A)1/n+λn​(B)1/n.
(1)
It also holds for compact sets and in standard measurable-set formulations with the appropriate measurability qualification. Normalize both volumes to one and apply the Prékopa–Leindler inequality to indicator functions.

Affine geometry

Words: 479 Articles: 10
Geometry and topology OurBigBook.com
The geometry of affine spaces, studying incidence and parallelism without choosing an origin or a metric.

Affine space (A)

Words: 464 Articles: 9
Affine geometry OurBigBook.com
A nonempty set A equipped with a group action of the additive group of a vector space V, such that for every x,y∈A there is a unique v∈V with x+v=y. There is no distinguished origin. Choosing one identifies A with V; changing it gives a translation.

Affine independence (∑i​λi​pi​=0, ∑i​λi​=0 ⟹ λi​=0)

Words: 81
Affine space OurBigBook.com
Points p0​,…,pk​ in an affine space are affinely independent if the only affine dependence displayed above has all coefficients zero, using any choice of origin to read the vector equation. Since the coefficients sum to zero, replacing the origin leaves that equation unchanged. Substituting λ0​=−∑i=1k​λi​ shows that this condition is equivalent to linear independence of p1​−p0​,…,pk​−p0​. It also says that an affine combination of the points has unique coefficients. In Rn, at most n+1 points can be affinely independent; n+1 such points span a full-dimensional simplex.

Integer lattice (Zd)

Words: 33
Affine space OurBigBook.com
The points with integer coordinates in a real d-dimensional affine space with a chosen origin and coordinate basis. Translations by integer vectors and dilations by positive integers preserve this set. The Gallai theorem for an integer lattice concerns finite colourings of these points and homothetic copies of finite configurations of them.

Homothetic copy of a finite configuration (a+tF,t>0)

Words: 40
Affine space OurBigBook.com
A translation and positive uniform scaling of a finite configuration F in a real vector space. It preserves the ratios and directions of differences between its points. In an integer lattice, the Gallai theorem for an integer lattice guarantees a monochromatic homothetic copy of every finite pattern in any finite colouring, with positive integer scaling factor.

Affine combination

Words: 56
Affine space OurBigBook.com
An affine combination of points Pi​ is ∑i​ai​Pi​ with ∑i​ai​=1, allowing negative coefficients. It is independent of the choice of origin: translating every point by T translates the result by T. It also commutes with every affine map. When all coefficients are nonnegative, it is a convex combination, placing the result inside the convex hull of the points.

Affine map (x↦Ax+b)

Words: 141 Articles: 2
Affine space OurBigBook.com
A map between affine spaces whose difference map is linear. After choosing origins it is x↦Ax+b, where A is its linear part of an affine map and b its translation. This definition allows noninvertible maps; invertibility requires A invertible.
Euclidean similarity (S(x)=cRx+b)
Words: 70
Affine map OurBigBook.com
A Euclidean similarity is a map S:Rn→Rn satisfying ∣S(x)−S(y)∣=c∣x−y∣ for a fixed c>0. It has the form S(x)=cRx+b with R orthogonal: after subtracting S(0) and dividing by c, the map fixes zero and preserves distances, hence inner products by polarization, so it is a linear orthogonal map. It is a contraction if c<1. Contracting Euclidean similarities define self-similar compact sets; the open set condition is a useful separation hypothesis for computing their Hausdorff dimension.

Affine map OurBigBook.com
The map A associated with an affine map x↦Ax+b; it is independent of the translation b. An affine Euclidean isometry has an orthogonal linear part, and an isometry between flat tori has a lift whose linear part carries one Euclidean lattice onto the other.

A closed half-space consists of a hyperplane and one of its two sides in a real affine space. Replacing the weak inequality by a strict inequality gives an open half-space. Half-spaces are convex sets, and finite intersections of closed half-spaces are linear polyhedra.

The moduli space of unmarked compact genus-g Riemann surfaces. For g≥2 it is the quotient Tg​/Mod(Sg​) of Teichmüller space by the mapping class group, with its quotient topology. The thick subsets are compact by Mumford's compactness theorem.

For stable compact Riemann surfaces with n distinct labelled marked points, where 2g−2+n>0, the displayed complex dimension counts independent conformal shapes and positions after conformal automorphisms are removed. On the sphere it is n−3, since three points fix a Möbius transformation. On a torus it is 1+n−1=n: one shape modulus and n positions, less one translation. For genus g≥2, the unmarked shape dimension is 3g−3 and continuous conformal automorphisms vanish. The shape dimension also follows from the Riemann-Roch theorem applied to holomorphic quadratic differentials.

For a cooriented integrable codimension-one distribution, choose a nonvanishing defining form ζ and an auxiliary form with dζ=η∧ζ. Changing the auxiliary form to η+aζ changes η∧dη by −d(adζ). A leaf is a maximal connected integral manifold of the smooth constant-rank integrable distribution defining a regular foliation. A closed transversal is a closed curve everywhere transverse to the leaves of a foliation. A single such curve meeting every leaf proves that the foliation is a taut foliation.

Orbifold OurBigBook.com
The orbifold fundamental group records loops together with their local isotropy relations, so a loop around a cone point of order m has its mth power trivial rather than being trivial itself. For an oriented closed surface of genus g with cone orders m1​,…,mr​, its presentation is ⟨a1​,b1​,…,ag​,bg​,c1​,…,cr​∣cimi​​=1, ∏j​[aj​,bj​]c1​⋯cr​=1⟩. A torsion-free finite-index subgroup of a hyperbolic surface orbifold gives a smooth locally isometric surface cover. The absence of torsion means that the subgroup meets no nonidentity local cone stabilizer.

Paired-polygon construction of finite surface covers

Words: 303 Articles: 3
Orbifold fundamental group OurBigBook.com
Pair the 2s edges of an oriented hyperbolic polygon by length-preserving identifications reversing their boundary directions. Label the pairs by generating elements A1​,…,As​ of a finite group T. Glue the corresponding edge of a copy labelled g to its mate in the copy labelled gAk​. Left multiplication of labels defines the T action. A vertex cycle of a paired polygon has angle sum θj​ and accumulated gluing word Cj​∈T of order qj​; above it lie ∣T∣/qj​ vertices, each of cone angle qj​θj​. The action is free away from vertices, and the vertex stabilizers are conjugates of ⟨Cj​⟩. If the base cone has integer order mj​=2π/θj​ and qj​∣mj​, this is an orbifold covering, with lifted cone order mj​/qj​. The lift is smooth exactly when qj​=mj​.

These are different covering maps.

A vertex cycle of a paired polygon is an equivalence class of vertices under the edge identifications. Its angle sum is the total angle at the resulting point of the quotient surface. Over a cone point of order m, a cycle of length ℓ in the monodromy on sheets has ramification degree ℓ and residual cone angle 2πℓ/m. Equivalently the subgroup defining the cover meets no conjugate of a nonidentity power of a cone generator.

Conformality

Conformal map OurBigBook.com
The local angle-preservation property of a conformal map. At a regular point its derivative is a positive scaling times an orthogonal linear map. Consequently composition multiplies gradient lengths by that scaling, as follows directly from the chain rule.

Conformal map OurBigBook.com
Two intersecting circles bound a lens. A Möbius transformation sending their intersection points to zero and infinity sends the two boundary arcs to rays, and the lens to a sector. A suitable power straightens the sector to a half-plane. The chosen sector and its branch must be identified by an interior test point; merely squaring an arbitrary boundary-straightening map need not be injective on the intended domain. A Cayley transform then gives a conformal bijection to a disc.

Conformal geometry

Words: 391 Articles: 5
Conformal map OurBigBook.com
Conformal geometry studies a metric tensor only up to multiplication by a nowhere-zero positive scalar function on a real slice. A conformal class determines angles in Riemannian signature and null directions in Lorentzian signature. The complexified flat four-dimensional conformal geometry is encoded by the Klein quadric, whose incidence relation describes null separation.

Words: 41
Conformal geometry OurBigBook.com
An equivalence class of Riemannian metrics under multiplication by positive smooth functions. Such rescalings preserve angles. On an oriented smooth surface, a conformal structure is equivalent to a complex structure, with local holomorphic coordinates in which its metrics are positive multiples of dx2+dy2.

Conformal compactification

Words: 303 Articles: 3
Conformal geometry OurBigBook.com
A conformal compactification realizes a noncompact metric space as a dense open subset of a compact space whose metric on that subset is conformally related to the original one. Its smoothness and boundary interpretation depend on the example. Conformal compactification of Euclidean space adds one point to four-space; Projective Minkowski compactification adds a null cone. A regular null-boundary conformal completion and a projective compactification need not have the same global topology or causal covering convention.
Conformal boundary (g​=Ω2g,Ω=0,dΩ=0)
Words: 80
Conformal compactification OurBigBook.com
A boundary obtained by extending the rescaled metric g​=Ω2g smoothly and nondegenerately to a hypersurface on which Ω vanishes with nonzero derivative. Its causal character is measured using the extended Lorentzian metric, not the divergent physical metric. In signature (+−−−), a timelike normal makes the boundary spacelike, a spacelike normal makes it timelike, and a null normal makes it null. These cases lead to different causal and initial-value properties. The conformal cylinder of two-dimensional de Sitter spacetime has spacelike past/future boundaries; the conformal strip of two-dimensional anti-de Sitter spacetime has two timelike boundaries.

Conformal compactification OurBigBook.com

Multiplying its flat metric by 4/(1+∣x∣2)2 gives the round metric, which extends smoothly over the added point. In the Klein quadric description, the compact space is the projectivized real null cone of signature (1,5). It differs topologically from Minkowski conformal compactification.

Conformal compactification OurBigBook.com
The Projective Minkowski compactification has infinite cyclic fundamental group, while the conformal compactification of Euclidean space is S4 and simply connected. Thus the affine substitution t↦it cannot extend to an invertible smooth identification of these real compactifications. Both are real slices of the same complex Klein quadric, which permits local analytic continuation without equating their global real topologies.
In affine cone coordinates [U,V,t,x] with 2UV+t2−∣x∣2=0 and U=1, the substitution is represented on the complex quadric by the rational map [U,V,t,x]↦[U2,UV+t2,iUt,Ux]. It preserves the quadric equation but is indeterminate at some infinity points, including [0,1,0,0]. This is a direct algebraic manifestation of the obstruction to a global regular Wick map.

Thus the spiral and disk form separate path-connected components.

If I were outside the convex cone generated by the contact matrices, a separating hyperplane would give a symmetric matrix A with trA>0 and ⟨Au,u⟩≤0 at every contact. Finite spectral matching by polynomial invariants
Words: 127
Buser finite length spectrum theorem OurBigBook.com
Suppose a compact parameter set carries a locally finite countable multiset of positive quantities, and a fixed injective transform of each labelled quantity is a polynomial in finitely many ambient coordinates. Assume only finitely many labels can have bounded value anywhere in the compact set. Then a uniform finite initial multiset determines the entire multiset. For each source label there are finitely many possible matching labels. Equality for finitely many labels in both directions is a finite union of algebraic sets, obtained from injective matchings and polynomial equalities. These algebraic sets decrease as more labels are included, so they stabilize by the Hilbert basis theorem. A compatible infinite matching in each direction follows by the König infinity lemma, and local finiteness makes multiplicities equal. Squared traces of hyperbolic holonomy representations give the application to the Buser finite length spectrum theorem.

A real Möbius transformation represented by A∈SL2​(R) with ∣trA∣>2. It has two fixed ideal boundary points and translates along the geodesic joining them; its hyperbolic translation length is 2arcosh(∣trA∣/2). Conjugating by a real Möbius transformation puts it in the form z↦eℓz with ℓ>0; its axis is then the imaginary axis.

Every orientation-preserving isometry of the Poincaré half-plane model lies in PSL2​(R). Every orientation-reversing isometry is the composition of one of these with the hyperbolic reflection z↦−z in the imaginary axis. Equivalently, the full isometry group consists of real Möbius and anti-Möbius transformations, modulo nonzero scalar matrices.

PSL2(R) OurBigBook.com
The group PSL2​(R) acts transitively on pairs (ℓ,P) consisting of a hyperbolic line and a point on it. Send the two ideal endpoints of ℓ to 0 and ∞, then use a positive dilation to move the resulting point on the imaginary axis to i.

Hyperbolic reflection

Words: 166 Articles: 2
Poincaré half-plane model OurBigBook.com
Reflection in a hyperbolic line is the unique orientation-reversing hyperbolic isometry fixing that line pointwise. The product of reflections in intersecting lines is a rotation through twice their angle.
Every hyperbolic-plane isometry is a product of at most three reflections
Words: 80
Hyperbolic reflection OurBigBook.com
A reflection in the perpendicular bisector of a point and its image corrects that point. A second bisector reflection through the corrected point can correct another point without moving the first. An isometry fixing two distinct points is either the identity or reflection in their joining geodesic: points with prescribed distances from both centres have at most two possibilities, exchanged by that reflection. Fixing a third noncollinear point then fixes every point. This constructs a factorization with at most three hyperbolic reflections.
Composition of reflections in ultraparallel hyperbolic lines
Words: 57
Hyperbolic reflection OurBigBook.com
The composition of hyperbolic reflections in two ultraparallel hyperbolic lines has infinite order. Map their common perpendicular to the imaginary axis in the Poincaré half-plane model. The two reflecting hyperbolic lines become semicircles centred at zero, with distinct radii r1​,r2​. Reflection in the radius-r semicircle is z↦r2/z, so their composition is z↦(r2​/r1​)2z. Every positive power remains nonidentity, because (r2​/r1​)2k=1 for k≥1.

For curvature minus one, no hyperbolic triangle contains an open hyperbolic disc of radius greater than 21​log3. Move the disc centre to zero in the Poincare disc model and enclose the triangle in an ideal triangle with the same radial vertex directions. One gap between ideal directions is at least 2π/3. Its opposite geodesic is at distance at most 2artanh(2−3​)=21​log3 from zero. The symmetric ideal hyperbolic triangle attains the bound as its inradius.

An included angle instead determines the third side by the cosine rule.

Hyperbolic triangle OurBigBook.com
Three corresponding side lengths determine a hyperbolic triangle up to an isometry of the hyperbolic plane. First match an ordered pair of vertices by an isometry. The third vertex lies at the intersection of two prescribed hyperbolic distance circles. There are at most two choices, interchanged by reflection in the geodesic through the matched pair; either choice can therefore be matched.

In curvature −1, a regular n-gon of circumradius R>0 has interior angle α(R)=2arctan(cot(π/n)/coshR), by the right-triangle angle form of the hyperbolic law of cosines. Thus its hyperbolic polygon area is (n−2)π−nα(R), continuously and strictly increasing from 0 to (n−2)π. Every area in that open interval is therefore attained at exactly one circumradius.

Cobordism

Words: 964 Articles: 19
Geometry and topology OurBigBook.com
A cobordism from a closed oriented n-manifold X0​ to X1​ is a compact oriented (n+1)-manifold W whose oriented boundary is −X0​⊔X1​.

Witt bordism (ΩnWitt​)

Words: 261 Articles: 3
Cobordism OurBigBook.com
Two closed oriented rational Witt spaces are Witt bordant if their signed disjoint union is the collared boundary of a compact oriented Witt space with collared boundary. Disjoint union gives the bordism group ΩnWitt​.

Witt null-bordism in dimensions one two and three

Words: 84
Witt bordism OurBigBook.com
Every odd-dimensional closed oriented Witt space bounds its closed cone: the new vertex has odd-dimensional link, so introduces no Witt obstruction. For a closed oriented two-dimensional pseudomanifold, normalize to a surface, fill each surface component by a handlebody, and attach a collar of the original space using the finite normalization map. Along the singular collar arcs the links are unions of circles; at their interior starting points the links are wedges of two-spheres. These links have zero middle intersection homology, so the construction is a three-dimensional Witt null-bordism.

Witt bordism classification

Words: 148 Articles: 1
Witt bordism OurBigBook.com
For k≥1, the rational middle intersection pairing induces an isomorphism Ω4kWitt​≅W(Q). The restriction k>0 matters: the degree-zero group is Z. In positive dimension congruent to zero modulo four, a space is Witt null-bordant precisely when its middle intersection form is metabolic.
Metabolic intersection form of a four-dimensional product
Words: 103
Witt bordism classification OurBigBook.com
A nontrivial product of positive-dimensional closed oriented Witt spaces of total dimension four has metabolic rational middle intersection form. For dimensions 1+3, the two Künneth summands in degree two pair only with one another, so either is a half-dimensional isotropic subspace. For dimensions 2+2, the outside degree-two summands pair with one another, and the IH1⊗IH1 summand has the tensor pairing of two symplectic forms. A Lagrangian in the first symplectic factor tensored with the entire second factor is a half-dimensional isotropic subspace of that summand. Adding one outside summand gives a Lagrangian in the complete middle form. The Witt bordism classification then makes the product null-bordant.

Trivial cobordism (M×[0,1])

Words: 41
Cobordism OurBigBook.com
A cobordism is trivial when it is diffeomorphic to a cylinder with the prescribed incoming boundary identification. Both boundary inclusions are homotopy equivalences and its relative homology with respect to either end vanishes. It can have critical points for a chosen cobordism Morse function; those must form an acyclic relative Morse chain complex.

H-cobordism ((W;M0​,M1​))

Words: 84 Articles: 1
Cobordism OurBigBook.com
A compact smooth cobordism is an h-cobordism when both boundary inclusions Mi​↪W are homotopy equivalences. The name does not itself impose simple connectivity. A trivial cobordism is an h-cobordism because a product cylinder retracts onto either end.

H-cobordism theorem

Words: 52
H-cobordism OurBigBook.com
A compact smooth h-cobordism of dimension at least six between connected simply connected closed manifolds is diffeomorphic to a product, relative to its incoming boundary. The boundary manifolds consequently are diffeomorphic. The dimension and simple-connectivity hypotheses are sufficient conditions, not necessary properties of a product cylinder. The two boundary inclusions being homotopy equivalences are necessary for a trivial cobordism.

Words: 95 Articles: 1
Cobordism OurBigBook.com
Framed cobordism is the generalized cohomology theory of stable cohomotopy. Its geometric maps have a stable framing of a vector bundle on their normal data. A finite covering has canonically framed zero-dimensional relative tangent data; its Gysin class of 1 is the stable transfer of the cover. A trivial d-sheeted cover gives d⋅1 in degree zero.

Words: 47
Framed cobordism OurBigBook.com
The degree-zero framed cobordism class is defined by the transfer of the subset cover of a framed vector bundle. With the canonical relative framing it equals (kn​)⋅1 for a globally ordered framing of rank n. Put l0​=1 and lk​=0 outside the rank range. Disjoint-union additivity and fiber-product multiplicativity of transfer give lk​(η⊕ζ)=∑i+j=k​li​(η)lj​(ζ).

Words: 382 Articles: 7
Cobordism OurBigBook.com
Complex cobordism is the generalized cohomology theory represented by the stable Thom spaces of universal complex vector bundles. Its geometric cycles use maps with chosen stable complex normal data. Its complex Thom classes give Chern classes in complex cobordism, and proper oriented maps have a Gysin map in complex cobordism.

Words: 53
Complex cobordism OurBigBook.com
The displayed product applies when k+m≥n. Move one projective subspace by a unitary isotopy into transverse position. The intersection is a linear projective subspace of dimension k+m−n, with normal complex bundle the sum of the restricted input normal bundles. If k+m<n, representatives can be made disjoint and the product is zero.

Words: 47
Complex cobordism OurBigBook.com
Pulling the external product of two normally complex submanifolds back along the diagonal gives their transverse intersection. Its normal complex structure is the direct sum of the restricted normal complex structures. Multiplication of Thom classes for a direct sum identifies this geometric representative with the cup product in complex cobordism. Empty intersection represents zero.

For a rank-r real bundle with chosen stable complex normal orientation, the complex-cobordism Thom class gives the displayed isomorphism by a↦π∗auξ​. Complex orientation of a smooth map

Words: 159 Articles: 2
Complex cobordism OurBigBook.com
Represent a map f:X→Y by a smooth map, embed its graph into Y×RN, and specify a stable complex structure on the normal bundle of that embedding, with the standard framing on the auxiliary real coordinates. Stabilization and homotopy identify equivalent choices. The auxiliary dimension is chosen to make the normal rank even; odd relative dimensions use an extra real suspension coordinate. The resulting oriented stable normal data defines the Gysin map in complex cobordism.

For a proper map with fixed complex normal orientation, apply the Thom isomorphism in complex cobordism, pull back by the collapse of a tubular neighborhood of a graph embedding, and desuspend the auxiliary Euclidean coordinates. The degree increase is the relative real codimension. Changing the orientation can change this map.

Restricting the tubular-neighborhood collapse of an embedding back to its source is the normal bundle's zero section. The Thom isomorphism in complex cobordism therefore makes pullback after the Gysin map multiplication by the Euler class in a generalized cohomology theory. For an actual complex normal bundle this is its top Chern class in complex cobordism.

The Milnor-Novikov coefficient theorem identifies the coefficient ring of complex cobordism as the displayed graded polynomial ring. In cohomological grading it has no positive-degree or odd-degree coefficients. Homological grading reverses the signs: MU∗​ has polynomial generators in degrees 2i.

An oriented knot cobordism is a compact oriented smooth surface properly embedded in S3×[0,1] with prescribed knots at its incoming and outgoing boundary. A connected genus-zero knot cobordism between knots is a knot concordance. Composing knot cobordisms adds their genera.

Geometry and topology OurBigBook.com
Chern-Weil theory constructs closed characteristic forms by applying invariant polynomials to the curvature of a connection.

Pontryagin class (pk​(E)=(−1)kc2k​(E⊗R​C))

Words: 69
Chern-Weil homomorphism OurBigBook.com
For a real vector bundle E, its Pontryagin classes are the even-index Chern classes of its complexification with the displayed alternating signs. They lie in integral cohomology of degrees 4k and obey a total-class product formula under direct sums. If a metric connection on a vector bundle has curvature matrix R, its first real representative is p1​(E)=−tr(R∧R)/(8π2). The Bianchi identity makes this representative closed, and Chern-Weil connection transgression makes its de Rham cohomology class independent of the connection. This normalization gives degree-four A-hat form −p1​/24.

A-hat form (A(R)=det1/2(sinh(R/(4πi))R/(4πi)​))

Words: 80
Chern-Weil homomorphism OurBigBook.com
For the vector-bundle curvature matrix R of a metric connection on a vector bundle on a real oriented vector bundle, the A-hat form is the even differential form defined by the displayed finite-degree power series, with square root having constant term one. The expression is independent of the choice of orthonormal frame. Equivalently, for formal paired curvature Chern roots ±xj​, it is ∏j​(xj​/2)/sinh(xj​/2). The Bianchi identity makes it closed, and changing the connection changes it by an exact differential form via Chern-Weil connection transgression. Its degree-four part is −p1​/24, where p1​=−tr(R∧R)/(8π2) is the first Pontryagin class form.

Thus the Chern-Weil theory four-form changes by an exact differential form, and its integral on a closed four-cycle is connection-independent. For a general unitary bundle, include the corresponding trace-product term in the Second Chern form.

NCS​[A]=−8π21​∫Σ​tr(A∧dA+32​A∧A∧A).

Chern-Simons 3-form OurBigBook.com
